# Chapter Three: Order of the Dragon

The sound of the old bronze bell echoed through the hallways of the old structure snapping Marcus from a sound sleep, he had only been at the old keep for fourteen hours. He sat up the down stuffed mattress tht sat upon the latticework of rope was mostly comfortable and definitely more comfortable then the platform he had gotten used to sleeping on at the farm he thought and then it was there.

Thoughts of Orah, he could still see the smile on her face as the vision of the woman he loved still echoed with pain. With an effort of will he pushed it back into the darkness of his subconscious, but not before it caused the same bone deep ache, he felt everytime he thought of her. The room he found himself in was a simple thing, a square ten by ten stone cube with a bed, dresser, desk and lamp.

Someone had put up a curtain and painted a picture of green grass and the sun. Since the building was completely underground most of the place had a hint of a claustrophobic feel. But the little things like the portrait and curtain went along way to curbing that. Marcus walked across the room, the stone floor was bone chillingly cold and he sped up a little until his feet met the thick white fur carpet that covered the center of the room. Reaching into the hand lathed standup dresser he found eight of the leather uniforms, all black as well as simple cotton shirts complete with drawstrings and cotton underwear and socks. Looking at the set, he could tell they were hand made the stitching wasn’t off by that much but enough you could tell a machine had not made these.

However instead of lending a disheveled or poor construction feel to the items it actually gave them more of a personal homey feel he thought smiling as he appreciated them. Slipping on both the underwear and shirt. He then pulled out the soft leather uniform, with a growing curiousity he laid the leather uniform out on the top of the dresser so he could examine the runes etched inside it. Placing his hand on a rune he pushed a small amount of power ino it and watched it as the power followed the contours of the rune, moving from one to the next as he watched with intense fascination then he noticed something, pushing his face closer to the runes and examining a few, he could see the power as it guided itself around the lines and edges of the carged glyphs, at certain points it would look dim, as if didn’t know where to go or the curve or corner wasn’t as it should be. Marcus touched it again adding a little more power an watched as it flowed through the runes, then he saw it, the breaks. Places were the runes were not finished or had been chipped or even not drawn to the exact flow of the power. It was obvious once you look at it, he thought as he studied the few offending runes.

Looking around the small room he began to rummage through the drawers until he found a small knife, it looked like something you would clean your nails with or cut cheese he thought. Marcus carefully began to etch into the runs, widening a few at key places and creating steeper angles in other. Pushing power into it he smiled as the power wound through the runes evenly and four times as fast. The runes were glowing far greater then before he noticed and with a nod and a smile of a job well done, he pulled the leather outfit on and worked to get the buckles correct.

Looking into the piece of highly polished bronze that acted as a mirror allowing Marcus to adjust the uniform. He closed the dresser and made the bed, ensuring to close the door to the small bathroom. It was the little things that amazed him. Where he had an outhouse on the old farm this place had running water, using a gravity fed system and even a working toilet and shower, though the hot water was lukewarm at best he thought.

But beggars couldn’t be choosers. Leaving the room, he closed the door and found himself in a long hallway door like his lined both sides lending it a look like a dorm or hotel. They stretched for as far as the eye could see, each acolyte, Mage or Master Mage all having the same size room with the same furniture. Almost like a monastic setup he thought guiding himself north and towards one end of the expansive hallway. Marcus passed other uniformed people as he made his way down the hall, a pin on there breast that told everyone which speciality or guild they served at least according to Maelen he thought eyeing each as he passed them but not having the context or knowledge to understand what he was looking at.

The Order of the Dragon, the name which Maelen called the group of Mages, an order created to recruit, train and police those with the gift. But on his travels here he had learned that the Order was not one single happy family, everything here lived and died by the guild, each guild specialized in something and had for ages, the leader of the guilds each had a say In the overall running and laws of the place. Reaching the end of the hall, he stopped trying to decide which way he had come the night before when they had arrived, but it had been late and honestly, he had been a bit overwhelmed.

So, there he stood looking left and right as he wracked his brain as to which direction to go.

“You look very lost” came a female voice from behind, turning he found himself facing a short raven haired girl her wide smile brightened the very hall they stood in and he couldn’t help but smile back “Very much so, I was trying to find Maelen” he said not knowing if she even knew who that was.

But her eyes lit up with regocnition “Oh you are Marcus” she breathed excitedly “I heard he brought you in, my name is Dara” she said standing taller and extending her hand, Marcus grabbed her wrist and she did the same in the typical greeting. “Its good to meet you, Im kind of at a loss, how do you know who I am exactly?” he asked almost embarrassed. Dara brightened even more if that was possible “Word gets around that Maelen was leaving to bring in another recruit, and here you are” she said, and Marcus nodded

“So, what do you do here?” He asked realizing that probably sounded as lame to her as it did to him causing him to wince a little with embarrassment. But the young woman didn’t seem to notice as she brushed a strand of the black hair out of her face. Her light blue eyes a wonderful contrast to her olive skin and dark hair and were incredibly distracting.

Marcus thought doing his best not to stare like a creep at those eyes. “Aside from the unending training I am a scribe” she said excitedly and then her smile faltered a bit. “Sorry, I forgot not everyone gets excited by quniform symbols and its relation to our magic” she commented sheepishly. “wanting to save her from embarrassment but also interested in what he had seen of the strange symbols he quickly responded. “No, it is interesting, there is a lot I still have to learn about it, just right now, I think I should find Maelen before he thinks I ran out” he finished almost apologetically.

Dara nodded and motioned Marcus to follow. “So, I guess you didn’t get much of the tour when you got in last night?” she asked turning to glance at him. Marcus was busy taking in everything he could. Artwork stood on the walls, they were metal and crystal, they stood out from the wall reliefs of animals and fantastic creatures and as he looked, he could see runic symbols set in a pattern within the art, something about it drew him to them. “No, I just went to my room, if that is my room” he answered distractedly as his eyes went from portrait to portrait something about them keeping his minds attention.

Dara noticed his interest and quickly jumped in. “Our Magi create those, some of them have hobbies, these are Master Albion’s paintings, he is amazing” she breathed, and Marcus could hear the hero worship in her voice and smiled, In the absence of rock stars he thought. “They are incredible, why are they laden with runes though, its almost like a pattern” he began touching on something that he couldn’t quite grasp he thought passing another, this one stood from floor to ceiling standing close to twelve feet tall, the metal dragon relief with red crystal eyes and a set of five runes over its wings and back, swirling crystal fire looked almost real he thought, something about the runes kept drawing his eyes but his inexperience prevented him from understanding what it was, as if his interest was almost instinctual he thought.

“This is the living section; we all live down here its two floors of apartments in the far east section of the complex in case you need to find your way. Had you turned left instead of following me, you would have ended up at the stairs leading to the second floor of apartments” she finished pulling Marcus’s attention from the reliefs as he looked around trying to commit the area to memory and silently thanking himself he didn’t turn left, then he would have been really lost he thought. This place was going to take a while to get used to. Dara turned and ascended a set of stairs with Marcus close behind for two flights and then she hit the landing opening the large wooden door.

Marcus was pretty sure it would be a while before he could get around this place without a guide as he followed her through the door and into a cavernous room. Marcus looked in awe as at least fifty people in the leather uniforms walked past, each with a purpose and heading somewhere.

It looked like the main concourse of grand central station, complete with a cathedral ceiling that was three stories above their heads. “This is incredible” he breathed, walking through the crowd to stand near the center of the room and looking up. Dara came to stand next to him “This is the main part of the entire keep, from here you can get virtually anywhere” she began pointing down the south side of the large room where three sets of double doors stood.

“The first set is the dining hall, the second is the offices and administration and the third is the armory and training areas” she began and then pointed north where another three sets of large double doors stood.

“The first is the way to medical, classrooms and research areas, the second is the guild entrance, all of the guilds and guild offices are located there and the last is storage and manufacturing” she continued smiling as he studied each direction. “The set of large stairs lead to the master’s area, that is where they live and study up there” she said pointing to a set of stairs that spanned the length of a tractor trailer and split a story up to ascend both north and south. In the center, above the stairs main landing stood a large metal and crystal picture, similar to the smaller ones in the living area, this one showed another dragon standing on a battlefield with soldiers fighting below him. The wall relief stood two stories high, making the dragon loom over the entire area and again Marcus’s eyes were drawn to the five runes across the body of the dragon something about them drawing his attention, ensuring he focused on them, but he didn’t know why. 
“That is amazing” Marcus breathed looking at it.

Dara followed his eyes and smiled “Yes, Zathirs did that when he built the keep” she finished, and Marcus turned to her “Zathris?” he asked remembering something about the name from his talks with Maelen, but he couldn’t quite place it. She noded “He is the Father of the order and the reason we still exist” she said and then motioned for him to follow. She headed north through the first set of doors which opened into a large hall, though not nearly as large as the room making it seem almost cramped Marcus thought. Proceeding down the hall and watching as every few feet another large hallway shot off of the main. This place is like a maze he thought as Dara came to stop at a door.

The raised words said Medical next to the door and she gently opened it, peeking her head in. “Master Patrice is Maelen awake?” she asked as Marcus tried to look around her to see the person she was talking to.

“He is Dara, you may enter and bring Maelen’s new acolyte with you” came an older womans voice her tone was firm, but friendly and Dara opened the door allowing Marcus to step in. The voice belonged to a tall woman her face covered in laugh lines and framed by long steel grey hair. She smiled and Marcus returned it.

“Hello, Im...” He began but the woman stopped him “Yes, you are Marcus Gavin, the new initiate that Maelen went to retrieve, word gets around fast my dear” she finished smiling. Marcus shrugged sheepishly “Apparently” he answered. She motioned for them to come in and shut the door, walking over to a large desk she lowered herself into it and gestured the two of them to take a seat.

Marcus and Dara both took a seat facing her. “Who are you?” Marcus asked curious, this looked like a hospital room, but the woman was dressed as he was, but there was indication of a guild, which aside from himself was the first person he had seen like that. However, on closer inspection he saw a metal symbol on her uniform, it looked similar to a caduceus except it was two dragons wrapping around what looked like a staff weapon of some sort.

“I am the Master Healer for the order, however we are not many, so we don’t warrant our own guild, instead we are simply members of the administration here at the complex.” Marcus nodded looking at the symbol again.

“Like Medical Doctors?” he asked, and the woman looked curiously at him. “That is the second time I have heard that, the first being from Maelen himself and to answer your question after discussing it at length with him, no and yes” she began, and Marcus leaned forward deciding he liked this woman and smiled motioning her to continue.

“We spent ages studying how to heal the body, we know herbs and bandages but Marcus, we are mages we specialize our gifts to healing others” she finished, and he nodded thinking he understood. Maelen had talked about specializing or honing your gift allowing you to study a particular aspect of it, which made sense to him. No one could do everything he surmised.

“How is Maelen” Marcus finally asked, almost kicking himself that it wasn’t the first question he had asked, and Patrice smiled seeming to sense his guilt. “He is fine, the old dog was banged up pretty bad but whoever nursed him did a competent job and he will recover fully” she finished and Marcus thought back to the young girl in the cage and her parents who insisted on healing Maelen as payment for bringing back there little girl.

He had spent a few days in bed and when he had finally gotten up, he had been slightly limping but otherwise no indication of the wound that had nearly killed him. In fact, when the woman had inspected it, it had nearly been closed up. Marcus’s eyes narrowed as he thought about that and also the way the woman looked when she talked about him and decided to play a hunch. “How long have you two been together?” he asked and Master Patrice’s eyes widended a little.

“Talk about me did he?” she asked and Marcus shook his head “No, just the fact that someone taught him how to heal himself and everytime you mentioned his name you smiled, it seemed a good bet” he finished the other woman nodding in approval.

“So, what exactly does a Magical healer do?” he asked after seeing Maelen’s wound heal with such amazing speed it was something he had wondered if he could learn, maybe not as a specialization but just because it was handy, he thought.

Master Patrice sat back “Well, the simple explanation is like you move objects, we dedicate our will towards fostering the creation of white blood cells, knitting of cell structures, deadening of nerves during healing” she began and then stopped noticing the amazed look on Marcus’s face. “What Initiate Gavin, you think because we ride horses and carriages that we don’t understand basic body structure, DNA architecture or the fine points of Bacteria, remember where we come from, a lot of that knowledge isn’t lost, its documented and waiting for a time when we can create the tools we need to be able to bring it back” she stated and Marcus nodded. Most people had knowledge of how a wheel worked, but probably wouldn’t know that you had to build an axle to an exact size which would require building a lathe or delicate chisel first, it didn’t mean that they didn’t have the knowledge of the theory, just the lack of knowledge at machining the pieces they would need to bring it to life. “I think I understand, just surprised, sometimes its easy to forget that a lot of that knowledge isn’t lost” he answered apologetically.

“Well, look who made it down here, I see you found a guide” Came a familiar voice from behind Marcus. Smiling he turned to see Maelen standing in the doorway, he looked well rested Marcus thought nodding to his friend.

“How are you feeling?” he asked the old man gently. Maelen shrugged “Im getting old, other than that I feel great” he said limping over to where the three of them sat talking. “As much as I would like to sit around here all day, we have things to do, Patrice, I will see you later” Maelen said winking to the Master Mage who shot a disapproving look at the old teacher. “Do not push yourself, or you will answer to me” she finished, and he made a placating motion with his hands. “I wont” he said shooting her his most endearing smile as he pushed Marcus out the door, Dara followed as well. Once they had made their goodbyes and the doors shut behind him Maelen leaned on them and closed his eyes. “I love that woman, but she scares the hell out of me” he whispered and Marcus and Dara both stifled a chuckle. “Dara, I need to borrow my initiate for a while” Maelen said smiling to the young lady Dara nodded “I will catch up with you at dinner” she called to Marcus heading back up the hall. Marcus watched her go and then turned to the old man “Whats wrong?” he asked the smile disappearing from his face and Maelen just shook his head “Nothing gets past you does it” he answered and motioned for Marcus to follow. They walked down the hall a little way and then found an empty examination room. Entering Maelen shut the door and then leaned on it. “As I said when we met, we are not safe here, no one is to know where you came from, we are going to meet albion, once he is done with you we are leaving” he began and Marcus cocked his head at the old man “What do you mean how long and done?” he asked wondering where Maelen was going with this. “I don’t know, I trust him, but he didn’t give me specifics, you will have to ask him, Im sorry this place should be safe Marcus but something is rotten here and I don’t know what” he answered and Marcus could see how much it pained him to say it. “What is it he will give me that I need to stay here for” he asked but he already knew the answer. Maelen just nodded his head. “There is information here you need to know, training you need to have, Albion has access to it, once you have it we will go” he said Maelen lowered his head and looked defeated for a moment “Again, Im sorry this place isn’t the haven it should be, im sorry there are people who would sacrifice you to see their power enhanced, but over the generations the gift is dying, the power these people have is a shadow of what it once was and some of them would stop at nothing for a chance at having the abilities you posess” he said. Marcus understood, people were people and there were always those who would mask “for the common good” as a license for just about anything, justification was a powerful license he thought.

“Okay, what do I need to do” focusing the conversation. Maelen nodded “We will go meet Albion, he will get you what you need, that is all I know, I trust him implicitly Marcus” he answered and then a knock came at the door Maelen whirled on it and then slowling opening it Marcus watched the tension leave his body as Patrice came into the small room. “I know you are having a moment and explaining to young Marcus how he has to be careful and all, but Aster is coming down the hall” she said shooting a pointed look at Maelen and he cursed. “Okay, thank you honey” he answered giving her a gentle kiss as she left the room. “Let’s go, we are heading to the guild area, but first we meet the council chair, just let me do the talking” Maelen said and opened the door.

The two of them walked out into the hall to find a small precession of men dressed in maroon dyed leather outfits with silk robes. The dress looked important as they talked among themselves deep in conversation as the two approached the group. A short man with a head of thinning grey hair and a perpetually pinched expression stepped forward. Marcus figured he was the head of the council, as his robe was brighter than the others. “Maelen, I take it this is your new initiate?” he asked with a small smile on his face, Marcus noticing the smile never touched his eyes. Maelen nodded returning the smile. “Yes, Lord Aster, this is Marcus” he answered presenting Marcus to the head of the council. Aster looked him over, his eyes were calculating as they roved over him. “Well met Marcus” he said the comment almost as a dismissal as he turned back to Maelen. “There is word, the Empress is looking for one who landed, coming from the sky in a metal container, you didn’t happen to come across anyone or anything that might lend credence to this rumor?” he asked, his eyes glancing to Marcus and then back to Maelen.

Maelen shot the council chair a confused look “No Lord Aster, nothing like that has happened in decades as far as I knew” he said, and Aster just nodded again his eyes roving from him back to Maelen. “Well, we know the last time something like this happened, we missed out on finding someone with the Source, to be able to study one such as that would be… invaluable” he answered. “If one has landed again after all this time, we should be the ones to find them, don’t you agree?” Aster asked Maelen and he nodded enthusiastically “Of course Lord, might I organize and dispatch a few scouts to find out more information?” he asked him and Aster nodded casually “Sure, lets do that” he said and then waiving his entourage on they moved down the hall without another word.

Marcus watched as they walked on, Aster looking back and catching Marcus’s eye once “What the fuck was that about?” he asked annoyed at the man’s attitude and Maelen pulled him along. “Aster knows” he said, and a chill ran down Marcus’s back. “What do you mean he knows?” he asked Maelen. He could see the angry look on the old man’s face. “He knows, which means we don’t have much time” he finished and then quieted Marcus as they entered the main hall. They walked across the hall entering the door to the guild area and remained quiet as they reached a large door about halfway down the cavernous hallway.

There was no sign on the door or indication as to what was behind it. Upon entering Marcus almost stopped as he looked over the cavernous room, looking up he counted three stories of books, catwalks running over each floor as young initiates rushed along each walk retrieving or pulling volumes as they went. In the center of the chaos stood a stooped ancient man who looked to be close to eighty Marcus thought as he leaned on a cane directing the initiates as they took notes, copied volumes or looked for reference material. “Master Albion” Maelen called waiving to the old man. Looking up marcus could see the man only had one good eye, the other milky white with cateracts as he smiled and hobbled over to the two men. “Maelen, I see you found your prodigy among the wilds” he said still smiling. Maelen nodded and then looked around to see who might be listening. “Yes, but we have a problem Aster suspects who and what Marcus is” he said, and the old man’s smile faltered. “Well then, we don’t have much time” he stated motioning the two men to follow him.

He walked across the room as the two followed until he reached a large wooden door at one end of the room, one of the few places Marcus noticed that didn’t have a bookshelf across it. Entering the room, he closed the door behind them, and Marcus found himself standing in the middle of a large plush office with a huge mahogany desk, tables and bookselves. The volumes on these shelves looked much older than the ones on the floor. Marcus noticed another leather outfit, similar to what he was wearing laid out on one of the tables. Walking over he saw the runic symbols carved into it. Touching it he watched as power ran through them, the light glow showing him each symbol as they lit up, again he noticed the places where it dimmed or bled, looking over the table he noticed small metal knives and picked one up. He chose a symbol that was mostly dimmed and saw that someone had not connected a corner on it, he etched in the corner on the rune and smiled as the symbol lit up. Putting down the knife he turned to see the two men looking at him Maelen looked confused, but Albion smiled approvingly. “Let me guess you fixed it?” he asked, and the other man turned to him. “What are you talking about, how could he fix it, he hasn’t learned runic script yet” Maelen said and Albion waved a dismissive hand at him.

“I have only seen one other who could do that, but as soon as you picked up the knife I knew it, you can see the flow can’t you Marcus” Albion asked and marcus nodded “yeah the runes kind of glow and when they aren’t right, they dim, like power isn’t getting through it” Marcus said trying to describe what he saw. Albion nodded “It was more common when man returned to earth, in fact it was how they invented the runic script we use today, you Marcus are a RuneWright” the old man stated and Maelen’s eyes went wide.

“That’s impossible they don’t actually exist, do they?” he asked the old man and Albion shrugged. “I have known one, other then that I can’t say Maelen” he began as Albion came over to inspect the work. “But Marcus is correct, the rune was incomplete, and he fixed it, how else do you explain it” he asked and turned back to him. Maelen stroked his ample white beard for a moment. “We need to get him trained Albion, the damn crown Is looking for him, the territory is turning to shit and now Aster suspects what he is, we don’t have a lot of time and he has too much to learn” he said sounding defeated. Albion looked at Maelen. “Don’t worry, have faith, it will work out” he said and then grabbing Maelen’s arm escorted him out of the room “Go, you have things to do, I will work with Marcus, come get him for dinner” the old man said and closed the door after escorting him from the room. “I shouldn’t have come here” Marcus whispered taking a seat across from the large desk. He heard a chuckle as Albion came over and around the large desk, every step slow and deliberate as he pushed himself into the chair and reguarded marcus for a moment.

“Im sorry I could not come to you, but my age and infirmities prevented me from making the trip, Maelen was right to bring you, despite his misgivings, what you need is here Marcus” the old man began and before Marcus could ask what that was the old man held up his hand and reguarded him from across the desk “I am curious when you look at the runes, what do you see?” he asked leaning forward with interest. Marcus looked over at the piece the piece of leather “The runes glow, its like I can push a small amount of power into them and I watch as it runs through each rune” he said distantly as he recalled the twisting and snaking of the power as each individual rune lit up showing him how the power should flow through it.

“It’s a rare gift son, and one that will prove useful im sure” he began and then thinking about Runes Marcus remembered the relief portraits “The pictures in the halls, Dara said you did some” he asked, and Albion smiled. “The runes on them, you want to know why” he asked as if the old man knew and marcus shook his head smiling, I am drawn to them and I don’t know why. Albion got up and walked over to a shelf, reaching in he pulled a small metal square relief and brought it over to Marcus handing it to him Marcus appreciated the detail work as he reguarded a bird molded from metal coming off the portrait. Marcus again noticed the runes and studied them, this time he touched one and with a small force of will pushed power into it. As he watched the first rune began to glow as power snaked through it as he jumped to the second and then the third and finally the fourth rune. But to his amazement the final rune remained dark. “Whats wrong with it?” Marcus asked looking back to Albion who smiled knowingly

“These aren’t just pictures child, they are spells Zathris had the ability to bring these to life the ones that hang all over the keep are guard animals used in case the castle was attacked but not since Zathris has anyone been able to bring them to life, you see its some kind of runic combination, how the runes are activated is the key” he said leaning forward appreciating the piece of art. “Oh we still practice the art, even through none of us understand the magic to bring them to life, we follow the original instructions and it has become more of an art then a spell I guess” he finished. Marcus put the picture aside resolving to take a closer look when he had time. “So whats first Master Albion” he asked.

Ten minutes later Marcus found himself in the main room as the old man brought over a very old text and gently laid it in front of him. “I was expecting more spells and less homework” Marcus said a little annoyed as Albion smiled at him.

“Knowledge is power young man, this is the original journal of our founder, it might shed some light on who and what you are” he finished motioning Marcus to open the book. For the next few hours he studied the story of how the order came to be and the man who founded it. Marcus was amazed at the ingenuity of the first development of the runic script and how they came to understand that those with the gift sometimes had abilities that were unique to them.

Albion entered the room sometime later, Marcus was surprised to see that the initiates had gone and his eyes burned from spending too long reading under the dim light “How long have I been reading?” he asked Rubbing the sting from his eyes looking up he saw how tired the old man looked Albion shuffled over and sat at a chair across from him with a sigh he smiled at Marcus “Many hours young man, many hours, what have you found?” he asked leaning in. Putting down the book he stared at it for a moment, his thoughts searching for the right words “A lot of killing Albion, a lot of power plays, unfortunately its what I expect to see of humanity, maybe they were right to destroy us, no matter what happens we never learn, we always allow ambition and power to drive out nature and in doing so, so many deaths” Marcus trailed off shaking his head. Here he was, running from people who all sought to use him to gain yet more power, he had hoped that maybe this new age of man would have been different, but in reality, humans were humans they didn’t change he reflected.

“Since Orah died, I have been running Albion, I have been told that I have no place that I will be safe. I even have to worry here, a place meant for those like me” he finished, and Albion could see the frustration and fear. “I know, have you wondered why it is the technology you see around you is so backward, even for having to start over we should have been further then this, the simple answer is Magic, We have relied on magic allowing our ingenuity and discovery to focus on something we had not had before this. Now however magic is dying, year after year less people are born with the gift and what they have usually pales to the generation before.” He began looking over at the stacks of books that lined the room. “So many have leveraged what they have based on the power they have been able to accumulate and now they see it all fading Marcus, whatever justification they use, that is what I boil down to. You represent the power that is slipping through there fingers and they see you as a chance to finally gain an upper hand overall.” He finished and Marcus could see the shame on the man’s face. “But Maelen is like me, he landed too, he has the same powers I do” Marcus argued, and Albion shook his head again Marcus could see the sadness on the man’s face. “Not anymore young man, when Maelen landed he was like you and when he came to the order he volunteered to allow our Mages to study him, to try and find a way to bring back the power that was being lost” he started as the old man shifted uncomfortably and Marcus could see him wince in pain. “Unfortunately a rather ambitious Master Mage thought he had an answer and using crystals tried to transfer Maelen’s power unto himself, he was stopped and killed but not before he caused irreparable damage that we still to this day do not understand to Maelen, he has power, but nothing like he had” Albion continued.

“And even now there are those here, who would try it again and others who would turn you over to the Empress justifying it by saying it would save our order” Albion rose to his feet and began to pace as he talked. “Something has happened in the kingdom Marcus, the death of the Emporer has left the Empress unchecked, she is replacing the old guard with new powerful mages but whatever she has done, its something new, she is enslaving the population and using Magic to keep them in line. You represent a threat to that power and she will stop at nothing to possess you, but if she captures you, I have no idea what she will do with you Marcus, you canot let that happen, at all cost” he said leveling a severe gaze on the young man. Marcus locked eyes with the old man and knew what he was saying, understood what he meant if he was bout to be captured Albion wanted him to kill himself. A shallow breath escaped his lips as he thought about this, what had these people so scared about the Empress he wondered. He didn’t want to explore this subject “Why am I here Master Albion, why bring me here if there is such danger?” he finally asked. Albion didn’t speak, instead shuffling over to a cabinet pulled two glasses and a carafe, returning to the table he poured them both drinks. “Drink up Marcus, all will be clear soon” he simply said returning the carafe to the cabinet and closing it. Marcus downed the water and looked after the old man, seeing the pain in his walk. “I am so sorry my son, but I am dying and don’t have a lot of time so I can’t explain everything to you, but you are here for my knowledge” he said and suddenly Marcus felt odd, his eyes began to droop and like a dimmer switch had activated his sight began to dim. He fought it “What did you do to me old man” he slurred as his vision continued to go dark. “What I have to, to save us Marcus” he simply said, and Marcus’s world went black.

Marcus woke sometime later as rough hands shook him repeatedly. “What the fuck” he said his eyes opening as he still sat slumped in the chair. “We have to go, NOW” Came a commanding voice and Marcus looked up to see a worried looking Maelen standing above him. “What the hell happened” he asked looking around the room and finally seeing the slumped body of the Master Albion sitting across from him. A crystal headpiece on the table in front of him, along with a metal and crystal statue that stood in the center of the table pulsing with light. Reaching up he felt a something on his head and taking it off Marcus saw the same kind of metal and crystal headpiece, once he pulled it off the lights on the statue in the center of the table dimmed and went dark.

“What happened Maelen, is he dead?” Marcus shot at Maelen as he looked alarmed at Albions body. “He is, dammit he used the transfer machine, now I understand why he wanted us here, we have to go Marcus, they know who you are and they are planning on handing you over to the Empress to protect their own asses” Maelan said pulling on the groggy younger man as he got to his feet. Marcus was confused and not just at the words, his mind was. wrong looking around he began to pull quotes from books he had never read, stories and biographies as well as and understanding to information he had never even studied flashed across his consciousness “What the hell did he do to me?” Marcus asked still shaky on his feet.

Maelen looked him over, he could see the worry on his face as he did. “Albion used the knowledge transfer machine, its one of the best kept secrets of the guilds, when a leader is close to death, he can transfer his knowledge to another, thus protecting that knowledge, but doing it kills the person” he finished looking back at the old Master’s body. “Rest well my friend, you will be missed” he said softly, and Marcus could see the tears streaming down his cheeks. Marcus looked at his friend but was unable to form the words to consol him. His mind was chaos in motion as thoughts shot across his mind everytime he tried to follow one, three more erupted into his consciousness. “What the hell is happening to me?” he croaked, leaning on the table trying desperately to clear his head to no avail.

Marcus grabbed him, gently propping him up and moving him towards the door. “Your mind is acclimating everything that was given to it, Albion has given you all of his considerable knowledge, but it will be days before you are able to really understand what you have, normally you would rest during this time but we can’t do that right now, they are on their way down to take you into custody, we have to leave now Marcus, I fear I was wrong to bring you here, if they take custody of you I don’t want to think what that woman has planned” he finished and marcus could hear the fear in his voice, this bolstered his own resolve as he shook his head as if this might help clear his head.

Dragging the younger man along he made his way out of the archives and down the hall, the area was clear the time either too early or too late for the regular traffic. There footfalls echoed throughout the area as they made their way to the doors to the central hall. Marcus leaned on Maelen as they moved unable to stand on his own as vertigo threatened to pull him to the floor. “We are going to get to the main hall, Patrice and Dara will meet us and from there we will quietly make our way to the stables” he whispered speaking more to himself then Marcus the younger man thought as he maintained a tight grip on the older man’s shoulder. His mind was still chaos, unable to think or form a sentence all he felt was fear, the fear of one who was unable to do so much as stand much less defend himself against those that wished him incarcerated.

Entering the main hall Marcus realized It was still night outside as most of the hall was still bathed in black as they made their way across it. They got to within a few feet of the main doors when a shout came from across the hall. “You will stop” came the shouting voice as torches were lit and Marcus looked on as a group emerged from the shadows. Dara and Patrice held by guards directly behind them. Standing out front of the small group was Lord Aster, lord of the order himself stood there, torch held high as he reguarded the two men. “Maelen, I can’t believe you would try this; don’t you know, we do this to save the order, if we don’t hand over the fugitive then the Empress will descend upon these halls with troops, killing us all. Have you not seen the power she now weilds” Aster said as if trying to reason with a small child, the condescending tone clear even from across the wide expanse? “I can’t believe you would stoop to doing the bidding of a woman who has twisted the gift Aster, you damn well know she has been taking our initiates before we get to them and doing who knows what with them, and you have heard the stories of the demons she controls, have you lost your mind man” Maelen spat putting himself in between Marcus and the Lord of the Order.

Aster shook his head “Stand aside Maelen, I command you, this is now a matter for the council, this man will be remanded and turned over to the Empress for all our sakes” he said and with that the other mages around him before to move towards the two men. Marcus’s eyes wandered up, seeing the large metal relief dimly lit by the torches the men carried. He focused on the runes looking at them, studying them. “Movement, fire, armor, earth, spirit” he whispered naming off the meanings and then his mind began to flash with other facts remembering touching the one, how it had lit all but the last rune. The memory muddled by the other plethora of information diluting his mind. “It’s a combination” he said, his eyes widening as information on the paintings, as if he too had spent decades painting and studying them but now seeing them in a new light.

As the men moved in Marcus pulled power to him the others feeling it as he continued to fill himself and then extending his hand he concentrated, trying to push the thoughts and memories from his head as he picked out each individual run, pushing power to it and watching as not only the run but the surrounding relief began to coalesce and glow with energy. Finally, he pushed power to the last one, pushing his will along with it “Protect us” he whispered and Maelen upon hearing the words turned and looked curiously at him. Then men feeling the energy release, but no one seemingly effected moved faster emboldended by the lack of destruction. Aster had warned them this man was powerful, but mayhe he had been mistaken they thought, a smile forming on one as he began to realize this might just be easy after all.

Then the wall shook, mortar spilling from between the stones and falling to the floor as a rumble vibrated from above. Everyone looked up, but the area above them was black and then as they watched a silver scaled back crawled through the rafters, the men looking around until let out a whimper his hand extending shakily as he pointed to the wall behind the two men. Everyone looked and for a moment stood confused as the painting behind the two men stood blank. “Where is the dragon?” one said just before the large silver head of the dragon descended from above snapping him up in its jaws and disappearing back towards the roof. “Its alive” the other guard screamed, detaining the two men now forgotten as he bolted for the doors to the living area. Aster called after him in protest but before he could put a hand on the doors, a silver claw shot out grasping the man around the mid section and tossing him across the room, he flew over the heads of Lord Aster and his small group and slammed into the wall with a meaty slap. Marcus shook himself off, his mind clearing a little as he stood straight and casually walked towards the group across from them.

As he did the large silver dragon with glowing crystal eyes brought itself down behind Marcus and stood there stalward, smoke snaking from its nostrils as it stared menacingly at Aster. “Let them go” Marcus commanded, and the women were released, no one said a word as all eyes were fixed on the large silver beast, its skin gleaming in the torchlight. “How is this possible” Aster said taking a step back as the beast uttered a growl that shook the entire room. For a moment Marcus thought about how to answer the man and finally decided less was more and smiled a little as he leveled a menacing gaze at the Lord of the Order “Because I willed it Aster” he simply said and motioned for the woman to join him. They came over but cautiously as they too, wide eyed looked upon the metal beast.

“We need to go” Marcus said to Maelen who was also frozen in place, not believing what he was looking at “Maelen NOW” Marcus said, the words breaking the man out of his trance he quickly joined the three, Marcus pushed his orders to the beast and they left the order and ran as fast as they could to the stables. Before Marcus could make the stables, he collapsed to the ground, his small amount of resolve finally dissolving as hims mind descended back into chaos. Maelen carried the young man as the four of them made the stables soon riding out. Once they had left the area, the large Silver dragon crawled back into the portrait where it had resided for three generations and was inanimate once more. “Don’t just stand there GO GET HIM” he screamed at the guards who remained with him as they bolted for the doors, trying to catch Marcus and Maelen.
